question.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(6,6,2)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $4x-7y-4z=-26.$
question.worked_solution:
Let's start by picking a point on the plane. To do that, we simply substitute some concrete values for $x$ and $y$ into the equation and solve for $z.$ Let's choose $x=1$ and $y=2$ (though it doesn't really matter what values we choose). Solving for $z,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}4x-7y-4z & =-26 \\ 4(1)-7(2)-4z & =-26 \\ -4z & =-16 \\ z & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the point $Q(1,2,4)$ which lies on the plane.

Computing $\overset{\to }{PQ},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨1,2,4⟩-⟨6,6,2⟩ \\  & =⟨-5,-4,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We also need a normal vector to the plane. For any Cartesian equation of a plane $ax+by+cz=d,$ the normal vector is $n=⟨a,b,c⟩.$ So, for the plane $Π,$ we have $n=⟨4,-7,-4⟩.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(-5)\cdot 4+(-4)\cdot (-7)+2\cdot (-4)|}{\sqrt{{4}^{2}+(-7)^{2}+(-4)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-20+28-8|}{\sqrt{16+49+16}} \\  & =\frac{|\,0\,|}{\sqrt{81}} \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the point $P$ lies on the plane.
